title: Why Is Everyone Talking About SK Hynix Stock Right Now? | SKHY Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions (fetched on retry attempt 2 after bot-gating)
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc explains why SK Hynix is in focus: the stock is down about $80 from its near-term high and near its 52-week low, even though the business is booming with record operating income and margins. In its October investor update, management said demand growth across memory is significantly exceeding expectations, with enterprise and personal AI leading near-term demand and physical AI - autonomous driving and robotics - broadening it from around 2030 to 2033 as large-language-model growth slows. Supply cannot keep pace: leading-edge processes are complex and new fabs take years, so management forecasts industry supply constraints until 2030, and customers are signing longer-term agreements with price ranges and deposits - 14 key customers including major cloud providers. SK Hynix is raising 2027 capex significantly to expand leading-edge capacity. Oversupply risk is almost zero near-term, low single-digit percent in 2028, and rises in 2029-2031, but the physical-AI demand wave and a replacement cycle for 2024-26 components should absorb it. At a forward price-to-sales of 2.9 he calls it ridiculously cheap, his discounted-cash-flow value is $253, and he upgraded his conviction to medium - he is interested in buying even though he already owns Micron. Call: SKHY BUY reiterated.

calls.base_case: Supply cannot keep pace with demand; long-term agreements lock in visibility and de-risk capacity build-out; demand from agentic AI now, physical AI (driverless cars, robotics) from ~2030-2033 as LLM growth slows.
calls.bull_case: Cloud capex grows 60%+ in 2027 and AI data-centre infrastructure ~40% a year to 2030; the memory shortage extends and SK Hynix re-rates toward its $253 DCF value.
calls.bear_case: Oversupply risk is near zero near-term but rises to low single-digit percent in 2028 and higher in 2029-2031 if too much capacity is built; US regulation could slow data-centre builds.
